title: Research
text:
My research focuses on understanding territorial transformation processes — land use change, landscape fragmentation, urban expansion, and intensification of productive systems — and their effects on landscape connectivity, thermal regulation, and biomass and carbon storage in the Yucatán Peninsula. I integrate remote sensing data with spatial analysis tools, bridging ecology, spatial analysis, and territorial studies.
Core themes:

Territorial transformation dynamics and land use change in tropical and urban landscapes
Spatial structure of biodiversity and vegetation from a multiscale perspective
Spatial estimation of biomass and carbon using remote sensing and artificial intelligence

Cross-cutting approaches:

Spatial analysis and remote sensing as support for socio-environmental systems research
Systematic reviews and meta-analyses applied to ecosystem health assessment

title: Jorge Omar López-Martínez
text:
I am a researcher at CentroGeo affiliated with the Investigadores por México program (SECIHTI), based in Mérida, Yucatán. My work focuses on spatial analysis of tropical ecosystems in southeastern Mexico.
I integrate satellite remote sensing, GIS, and ecological modeling to understand landscape connectivity, carbon sequestration, and land use/cover change in tropical and urban ecosystems.
I also serve as Handling Editor for Frontiers in Forests and Global Change (Tropical Forests section).
